Governance review

Treasury and counterparties

Grants, compensation, asset trades and payments requiring further records.

What the payments represent

The reviewed records mix grants, scheduled compensation, reimbursements, protocol operations, locked allocations and asset exchanges. Each needs different evidence. A large LUNA receipt may be an OTC trade; a contract receipt may be liquidity deployment; a scheduled claim may relate to an earlier entitlement period.

Do not add upstream grants and downstream distributions twice. Do not describe recurring transfers as vote buying without an agreement, communications or other direct evidence.

Who funded the reported work?

ERIS’s 2025–2026 retrospective describes its products and operational work. The records identify the following Phoenix grants and external support.

The identified direct project grants total 265,000 USDC. Votion’s earlier Phoenix award predates the article’s October 2025–October 2026 period; excluding it leaves 215,000 USDC in grants initiated within that period. The 100,000-USDC liquidity allocation is separate capital, not another development fee.

Recurring Stewardship compensation is additional, but the record does not allocate it across each listed app or security task. Protocol fees and validator receipts also exist; their contribution to these development costs has not been reconciled.

These amounts are project funding, not personal profit. The Hydro grant covers separate work, so the two awards do not establish duplicate billing. The records do not support a reliable Treasury-versus-external percentage for all the work in the article.

The article’s current $1M TVL claim is not reproduced by the roughly $553,000 supply query or the market page. A different dated peak or TVL definition could explain it; the comparison does not establish that Creda never reached $1M.

Combined, the reviewed public-contract positions represent approximately 42% of supplied value. The remaining balance is not proven to be independent external demand. Queries were sequential, without one confirmed common block height, so the percentages are approximate.

At capture, the LUNA market had approximately 73.85% utilization and an 18.46% annual borrow rate. This shows borrowing at that time; it does not show demand throughout the year, the number of independent borrowers or whether development spending was justified.

Delivery and security claims

The 10,000-USDC Creda analytics payment is verified, but payment is not independent milestone acceptance. A dated unfinished page would not establish that no analytics work existed. AADAO separately reports Votion’s Hydro milestones complete and jointly verified.

Zero historical bad debt and every borrower remaining healthy throughout the year were not established by the aggregate query. Public audit reports exist, but coverage must be matched to each deployed revision.

The article’s approximately $10M security attribution was not independently substantiated as a dated dollar calculation. Cosmos Labs documents collective recovery of already-stolen assets and losses on the Hub side; that does not disprove contributions elsewhere. Prevented theft, recovery custody and final restitution are different outcomes.

Director compensation and October schedules

The 2026 coverage window records 57,096 USDC to MB, 66,480 USDC to Vini and 46,745.70 USDC to Rose under the report’s classifications. Vini’s total includes a 16,900-USDC audit payment and recurring infra payments. Rose separately received 237,323.047934 LUNA in an OTC trade supplying approximately 0.19657723 WBTC; that is not compensation.

October actions 118–120 created new Stewardship payments for 0xphilipp, Rose and MB, but not Vini. Separate infra actions continued. The chain record does not explain the omission.

OTC and related-party execution

The 50-weight ERIS signer received 795,991.566014 LUNA through Treasury offers 91, 106 and 111. The checked messages are execute_otc, so these are asset exchanges, not salary. The governance questions are price fairness, approval, disclosure and execution quality.

Other large OTC recipients must likewise be valued using the asset they supplied and execution-time prices. LUNA totals alone do not establish expense, gain or loss.

Records needed to reconcile payments

  1. Complete action exports: recipient, entitlement period, approval, claim, cancellation and transaction.
  2. Contracts, invoices and pricing for monthly validator transfers and the ERIS invoice to Rebel.
  3. Statements of work, competing quotes where relevant, measurable deliverables and independent acceptance.
  4. Related-party OTC terms, supplied assets, market-rate checks and execution timestamps.
  5. Beneficiary/decider overlap and recusal records for A159, A249, A266 and A271.
  6. Admin and owner powers over recipients, schedules, fees, code and future voting.
  7. Account continuity without assuming exclusive key custody; reconcile current and predecessor role wallets.
  8. Direct wallet-flow graphs that distinguish native transfers, CW20 transfers, contract operations and module accounts.
